widgets_values:
visual_style:
Late-1980s to early-1990s theatrical Japanese mecha OVA animation. Hand-drawn 2D cel animation with crisp inked outlines, carefully painted cel shadows and highlights, richly painted backgrounds, dense hand-drawn mechanical detail, strong graphic silhouettes, period-authentic anime color design, analog optical effects, and subtle film grain.

High-budget theatrical OVA production quality with mature anime character drawing, intricate mechanical draftsmanship, expressive traditional key animation, strong perspective drawing, dramatic composition, controlled cel-animation timing, and hand-crafted effects animation.

Mechanical surfaces use precise inked panel lines, layered armor construction, restrained cel highlights, mechanical joints, vents, warning markings, and detailed industrial design consistent with premium Japanese science-fiction animation from the era.

Effects use traditional hand-drawn animation language: cel-animated sparks, painted energy light, atmospheric vapor, speed smears, impact frames, mechanical vibration, hand-drawn motion streaks, painted smoke and clouds, and analog optical glow.

overall_audio_style:
Audio has the character of a high-budget late-1980s to early-1990s Japanese science-fiction OVA. Mechanical effects are weighty, layered and tactile: switches, relays, servos, hydraulic movement, metal impacts, cockpit vibration, engines, launch mechanisms, armor resonance and thrusters have distinct physical sound.

Dialogue remains clean and intelligible over action. Japanese speech uses natural dramatic anime performance rather than exaggerated caricature. Radio or cockpit communications use restrained electronic compression only when the speaker is actually transmitted through communications equipment.

non_diegetic_music:
Persistent retro OVA mecha score built from analog synthesizers, orchestral strings, brass-synth layers, tom-heavy percussion, low electronic bass and occasional atmospheric pads. Fast action uses driving rhythmic synth and percussion; large-scale or quiet orbital moments reduce into broad sustained orchestral-synth textures. Musical transitions follow the pacing of the sequence without changing the established musical palette.

id="x401"
duration_seconds: 11

A Japanese male combat pilot in his late twenties has a lean athletic build, short messy black hair and sharp dark eyes. He wears a fitted dark navy pressure suit with muted red shoulder markings, reinforced black boots, black gloves, compact grey chest life-support hardware, and a white flight helmet clipped securely at his right hip.

He is already sprinting at full speed down a long straight military spacecraft corridor. The corridor has dark steel wall panels, ribbed structural supports, exposed overhead conduits, repeating cool-white ceiling strip lights, small red warning lamps and yellow deck-edge markings. Approximately twelve meters ahead, the corridor physically bends ninety degrees LEFT around a broad permanent steel corner.

A medium rear three-quarter tracking camera travels forward approximately 1.5 meters behind the pilot and slightly to his right at waist-to-chest height, matching his running speed.

His torso leans forward, his arms pump naturally and his boots strike the metal deck rapidly. The white helmet clipped to his hip bounces with every stride.

As the left-hand bend approaches, the pilot keeps his head, shoulders and gaze aligned with his direction of travel.

He reaches the corner, plants his right boot near the outside edge, lowers his center of gravity and leans his entire body left. He runs continuously through the ninety-degree corner without stopping or looking around.

The tracking camera follows the exact same curved route. It physically arcs left around the steel corner while continuing forward, preserving approximately the same rear-right distance from the pilot.

Directly around the bend is a large rectangular mecha loading bay with a high industrial ceiling, overhead gantries, fixed service equipment, yellow-black hazard markings and a broad unobstructed floor.

At the far end of this loading bay, a colossal humanoid combat mecha already stands secured upright in a mechanical launch cradle. The mecha has white and pale-grey armor, a dark navy torso, muted red warning accents, heavy angular shoulders and a compact armored head.

A circular armored cockpit hatch is already OPEN in the center-front of its torso. The circular hatch door is hinged along its upper edge and raised above the opening. Two fixed handholds flank the opening and one fixed foothold sits immediately below it.

The pilot straightens from the turn and continues sprinting directly toward the waiting mecha.

He reaches the torso, grabs both existing handholds, plants one boot on the fixed foothold and pulls himself upward to the open circular cockpit.

Immediately inside the opening is a fixed forward-facing contoured pilot seat. The seat back faces toward the rear interior of the mecha, so the pilot must sit with his back entering first in order to face forward.

Still holding the handholds, the pilot physically rotates his entire body through 180 degrees. His feet and hips turn first, followed by his torso, shoulders and head, until his face points outward toward the loading bay and his back points into the cockpit.

He bends his knees and lowers himself BACKWARD into the opening.

His hips contact the seat cushion first. His back and shoulders then settle firmly against the backrest. He is now correctly seated facing the mecha's forward direction.

Two heavy restraint straps already hang beside the seat.

He grabs both restraints, pulls them diagonally across his torso and locks them into the central buckle with a hard mechanical CLACK.

Still seated in exactly the same orientation, he reaches upward with both hands to the existing inner handle of the raised circular hatch.

He pulls the armored hatch downward.

The hatch rotates down on its upper hinge, progressively covering the cockpit opening until the circular door meets the armored rim.

Multiple mechanical locking dogs engage around the circumference.

The cockpit hatch finishes completely CLOSED and SEALED.

overall_soundscape:
Rapid boot impacts, heavy breathing, spacecraft ventilation, distant warning electronics, brief boot friction during the running turn, large loading-bay machinery, metal handhold impacts, the pilot dropping into the seat, restraint hardware locking, the heavy hatch rotating shut, and multiple mechanical locks engaging.

non_diegetic_music:
Fast analog synthesizer bass pulses, aggressive tom percussion and short brass-synth accents intensify through the run and loading-bay approach, ending with a heavy musical accent as the hatch seals.

id="x402"
duration_seconds: 8

The shot cuts abruptly to the interior of the already-sealed humanoid-mecha cockpit.

The same Japanese male pilot is already seated correctly in the fixed forward-facing pilot seat. His dark navy pressure suit, red shoulder markings, black gloves and grey chest life-support hardware remain unchanged. The heavy restraint harness is already locked firmly across his torso.

The circular armored exterior hatch remains completely closed and sealed behind the pilot seat.

The compact cockpit contains dense dark-grey mechanical instrumentation. Existing physical toggle switches, guarded power switches, rotary controls, analog gauges and indicator lamps are built into fixed control banks to the pilot's left and right. Two heavy flight throttles are mounted beside his thighs. A wide curved forward display assembly is already installed ahead of him but begins mostly dark.

A low front-left three-quarter camera is positioned ahead and slightly left of the pilot near knee height, looking slightly upward. His face, upper torso, restraint harness and both control banks are visible.

The pilot immediately reaches to the existing left switch bank.

His gloved fingers throw four adjacent metal toggle switches upward in rapid succession.

CLICK. CLICK. CLICK. CLICK.

Small amber indicators beside those switches illuminate in sequence.

His right hand moves directly to the opposite control bank.

He flips open two existing red safety covers and firmly depresses the guarded switches beneath them.

Electrical relays activate throughout the cockpit.

Analog gauge needles sweep rapidly upward.

Rows of existing amber and green indicators illuminate in cascading sequences.

The camera makes a small slow push toward the pilot.

He reaches forward with both hands and grips two existing heavy main activation levers.

He braces his shoulders against the restraint harness and pulls both levers decisively into their powered positions.

The forward panoramic display illuminates from darkness with cool green-blue system graphics.

Cold display light washes across his face, gloves and pressure suit.

A deep mechanical power vibration builds through the seat and surrounding instrument panels.

Status lights stabilize.

The pilot releases the activation levers.

His left hand lowers onto the existing left flight throttle.

His right hand lowers onto the existing right flight throttle.

Both hands close firmly around the throttles while he continues looking directly forward.

overall_soundscape:
Metal toggle clicks, safety-cover snaps, guarded switch impacts, relay chatter, moving gauge mechanisms, electrical startup tones, rising turbine-like machinery, hydraulic pressure and steady cockpit vibration.

non_diegetic_music:
Rapid analog arpeggios and tightly spaced tom hits build through the startup sequence. Sustained brass-synth tones rise during the main power activation.

id="x403"
duration_seconds: 9

The shot cuts abruptly to a mechanically fixed camera mounted immediately BEHIND the pilot seat inside the same sealed and fully powered cockpit.

The same Japanese male pilot remains correctly seated and tightly restrained.

His spine is pressed against the seat back. His chest, face, knees and toes all point FORWARD in the same direction.

The camera is centered immediately behind and slightly above his shoulders.

The visible physical order from nearest to farthest is:

camera → seat back → back of pilot's head and shoulders → his forward-facing body → his hands and knees → panoramic HUD → launch tube.

Only the BACK of his short messy black hair, neck, shoulders, upper restraint straps, forearms and gloved hands are visible.

His face points away from the camera for the entire scene.

Directly ahead of him is an existing 180-degree wrap-around panoramic tactical HUD. The HUD is positioned on the same side of the pilot that his face, chest, knees and toes point toward.

It is a forward display rather than a reflective surface.

Beyond the HUD is the mecha's forward-camera view down a perfectly straight enclosed spacecraft launch tube.

The launch tube contains repeating dark structural ribs, bright white guidance lamps, parallel acceleration rails, yellow-black service markings and a distant central vanishing point directly ahead of the pilot.

Two existing flight throttles sit beside the pilot's thighs beneath his hands.

One existing illuminated red launch button is mounted forward and slightly to his right, between his seated position and the panoramic HUD.

For approximately one second, the powered cockpit vibrates gently while the pilot remains still.

Both hands hold the throttles.

He stares straight forward toward the distant vanishing point.

(S1) says: <d>[Japanese] システム、オールグリーン。発進！</d>

As the final word ends, his right hand releases the right throttle.

His right arm reaches FORWARD toward the existing red launch button.

He strikes the button once.

The button visibly depresses.

The mecha immediately accelerates FORWARD in exactly the same direction the pilot is facing.

The massive acceleration force pushes the pilot BACKWARD against his seat, opposite the direction of travel.

His spine and shoulders compress firmly against the seat back nearest the camera.

The restraint harness pulls tight across his shoulders.

His head moves slightly backward under the force but continues facing forward toward the HUD.

His right hand immediately returns to the right throttle.

Both hands grip the throttles tightly.

The cockpit enters intense high-frequency vibration.

Because the camera is mechanically mounted behind the pilot seat, the camera vibrates with the cockpit while preserving exactly the same rear-facing composition.

On the panoramic HUD, the distant launch-tube vanishing point remains centered.

Guidance lights and structural ribs rush from the distant CENTER of the forward view toward the pilot and sweep outward past the left and right edges of the display at rapidly increasing speed.

The velocity indicator climbs rapidly.

The central alignment reticle remains fixed directly ahead.

The camera stays behind the pilot.

The pilot continues facing forward.

The HUD remains ahead of him.

The launch tube remains beyond the HUD.

The machine continues accelerating in the exact direction the pilot is looking.

The scene ends with the pilot pinned firmly into the seat, both hands gripping the throttles, while the launch tube streams past ahead at extreme speed.

overall_soundscape:
Low powered-cockpit vibration, launch-button impact, a heavy initial acceleration shock, rapidly intensifying propulsion noise, structural rattling, restraint tension, panel vibration and increasingly powerful launch-tube resonance.

non_diegetic_music:
The action score briefly pulls back beneath the Japanese line, then surges immediately after launch with pounding percussion, rapid analog bass pulses and sustained high strings.

id="x404"
duration_seconds: 10

The shot cuts completely away from the cockpit to a very wide exterior orbital view.

A colossal dark-grey military capital spacecraft several kilometers long hangs in low orbit above a vast blue-white planet.

The ship is covered in layered armored hull plating, recessed launch bays, antenna structures, radiator surfaces, engine sections and thousands of tiny illuminated windows.

The blue-white planet curves across the lower portion of the composition. A thin luminous blue atmosphere follows its limb and enormous white cloud systems spread across the visible surface.

Black star-filled space surrounds both ship and planet.

The immense capital spacecraft stretches across the upper-middle frame.

The camera remains almost completely still for approximately three seconds.

The ship drifts only subtly relative to the distant stars.

Its tiny illuminated windows and recessed hull lights emphasize its enormous physical scale.

A single brilliant point suddenly emerges from a launch opening on the underside of the capital ship.

The launched object is so distant that its humanoid form cannot be resolved.

It appears only as a tiny brilliant moving point.

The object rapidly travels downward away from the vessel toward the planet.

The camera begins a slow large-amplitude TILT DOWN, following the descending point without rapidly zooming toward it.

The enormous capital ship gradually moves toward the upper edge of frame.

The planet occupies progressively more of the composition as the camera continues its slow downward tilt.

The tiny bright object approaches the planet's thin atmospheric limb.

As it reaches the atmosphere, a compact orange glow forms tightly around it.

The atmospheric glow becomes slightly brighter as the object continues downward while remaining extremely small compared with the planet.

The scene ends with the vast planet dominating the image and the tiny orange-glowing object descending deeper into its atmosphere.

overall_soundscape:
No diegetic exterior sound in the vacuum of space.

non_diegetic_music:
A broad sustained analog-orchestral chord replaces the rapid action rhythm. Deep synthesizer pads and sparse low percussion create a deliberate sense of orbital scale.

id="x405"
duration_seconds: 9

The shot cuts abruptly to a completely new exterior camera already descending at extreme speed through dense planetary clouds.

The first frame contains only layered grey-white cloud formations and cold blue daylight filtering through openings above.

Nearby vapor streams rapidly UPWARD across the image because the camera is plunging downward.

After approximately one second, a huge dark mechanical silhouette begins forming inside the dense cloud behind and above the camera's direction of travel.

The silhouette rapidly becomes clearer.

The same colossal humanoid combat mecha breaks through the cloud layer.

Its complete form becomes readable: compact helmet-like head with narrow luminous green visor, broad white and pale-grey armored shoulders, dark navy armored torso, muted red warning markings, two articulated arms, two articulated legs, heavy mechanical joints, vents and stabilization-thruster assemblies.

White atmospheric vapor peels away from its head, shoulders and forearms.

The camera continues descending ahead of the machine and performs a small-amplitude arc toward the mecha's front-left side.

It settles into a low front three-quarter tracking view several body lengths ahead of the descending mecha.

The camera matches most of its downward velocity, keeping the machine large and stable in frame while cloud formations continue streaming rapidly upward around it.

The mecha holds both arms slightly away from its torso for stability.

Its legs extend beneath and slightly behind its body.

Dense airflow strikes the armor.

Shoulder plates and exposed mechanical components visibly vibrate under atmospheric turbulence.

White condensation forms around the leading edges of the shoulders and forearms, stretches backward in the airflow and collapses.

Brief orange-red atmospheric heating flickers intermittently along the forward shoulder, forearm and lower-leg armor.

A powerful lateral turbulence pulse strikes one side of the mecha.

Its torso and shoulders yaw several degrees away from alignment while its articulated limbs respond physically to the force.

Compact stabilization thrusters on the opposite side fire short bright exhaust bursts.

The thrust corrects the machine back toward its previous descending orientation.

The Japanese pilot remains physically inside the sealed torso cockpit and is not visible from this exterior camera.

(S1) says: <d>[Japanese] 大気圏内。目標に接近中。</d>

As the radio line finishes, the mecha punches through another thinner cloud layer.

Vapor bursts outward around the shoulders and streams rapidly upward behind the descending machine.

The luminous green visor remains pointed along the direction of travel.

The camera maintains the same low front three-quarter tracking relationship while the mecha continues its hypersonic descent.

overall_soundscape:
Continuous atmospheric roar, severe wind shear, armor vibration, structural groans, turbulent buffeting, pressure changes while crossing cloud layers and short stabilization-thruster bursts.

non_diegetic_music:
Rapid tom percussion, low analog bass pulses, urgent high strings and sustained brass-synth layers drive the descent.

non_diegetic_music:
Rapid tom percussion, low analog bass pulses, urgent high strings and sustained brass-synth layers drive the descent.
